items.title: Cartesia ships Sonic-3.6, now #1 on both Artificial Analysis speech leaderboards
items.summary: Cartesia released Sonic-3.6 on August 18, just three months after Sonic-3.5, attributing the naturalness gains across 44 languages to fundamental model improvements built on developer feedback rather than a bigger model. It now tops both Artificial Analysis speech arenas — 1,283 Elo on the Provider Voice board and 1,123 on the Controlled Voice board, ahead of Sonic-3.5 and ElevenLabs' Eleven v3. Built on state-space models rather than transformers, Cartesia reports sub-90ms time-to-first-audio; it's in beta on Cartesia's API, with Artificial Analysis pricing it at roughly $49 per million characters versus $100 for Eleven v3.
items.whyItMatters: Sonic-3.6 landing at roughly half of ElevenLabs' per-character price while beating Eleven v3 on both naturalness and latency benchmarks makes it the most direct threat yet to Anna's ElevenLabs voice stack — worth a side-by-side latency/quality test.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with automatic age-prediction routing
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT for Teens globally starting August 18 for users 13-17, adding content restrictions (no romantic language, self-harm topics blocked) and homework support designed to guide rather than hand over answers. Anyone who states their age as under 18, or whom OpenAI's age-prediction system estimates is a minor, is automatically routed into the teen experience; the global rollout is expected to finish within two weeks.
items.whyItMatters: OpenAI's age-prediction and automatic account routing is a reusable pattern for any tutor app that serves both kids and adults — worth watching how they tune false positives given Romain runs on OpenAI's Realtime API.

items.title: AI inference chip startup Etched doubles valuation to $21B in a month
items.summary: Etched raised a $700M Series D led by Jane Street at a $21B valuation, up from $10.3B just a month earlier after a $300M Series C. The company builds specialized low-voltage prefill chips plus new memory and interconnect tech aimed at making AI inference faster and cheaper, challenging Nvidia; Jane Street is both investor and first customer, already running Etched hardware in production.
items.whyItMatters: Etched's entire bet is cutting inference latency and cost — the same constraint that determines how fast Romain/Anna can respond — so its hardware approach is worth tracking as a longer-term lever on real-time voice latency.
